key_insight: Guidance for diffusion and flow generative models should respect probability conservation on the learned data manifold; by formulating guidance through the continuity equation, the paper derives a probability-conserving adjustment that keeps samples on-manifold under strong guidance.
problem_solved: Heuristic guidance methods (e.g., Classifier-Free Guidance and velocity extrapolation) break probability conservation and push samples off the learned generative manifold when guidance is strong, degrading sample fidelity and consistency.
method: Analyze guidance as a modification of the generative vector field using the continuity equation to characterize how guidance redistributes probability mass.
Derive a corrective, probability-conserving guidance term (flow guidance) that modifies velocities/scores while preserving the continuity equation and manifold probability.
Implement the correction within flow- and diffusion-based samplers to produce on-manifold trajectories under strong guidance without heuristic extrapolation.
impact: Provides a principled, physics-inspired way to apply strong conditioning to generative models that maintains sample fidelity and probabilistic consistency, enabling more reliable controllable synthesis in applications requiring strong guidance.
visual_elements: Side-by-side manifold diagram: trajectories with standard CFG (leaving manifold) vs. probability-conserving flow guidance (staying on manifold).
Flow-field visualization: vector fields before and after applying the continuity-equation correction, with probability mass arrows.
Continuity-equation schematic: simple annotated equation linking divergence of flow to probability change, showing where correction acts.
Performance chart: qualitative/quantitative comparison (e.g., fidelity or realism metrics vs. guidance strength) showing stability of the proposed method under strong guidance.
paper_authors: Parsa Esmati, Junha Hyung, Amirhossein Dadashzadeh, Jaegul Choo, Majid Mirmehdi
